_README: THE SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH FOR WHO THIS BUSINESS IS. Every page footer, every policy page, the Merchant Center account, the Stripe account and the feed all read from here. They have to agree: Google's verification cross-checks the legal name, address and country across the website, the Merchant Center registration and the payments profile, and a mismatch between them is the most common reason a new account fails. Any field whose value is still null BLOCKS the build - preflight.py refuses, and that refusal is deliberate. Placeholder text on a live shop is itself a documented misrepresentation trigger, so an unfinished field must stop a deploy rather than ship as 'Your Company Here'.
_brand: The shop's trading name, e.g. 'Wonderleaf'. Used as the feed's [brand]. Allowed to be your own brand because you make the product (Google permits own-brand for private label/manufactured goods). Must be the same word used in the site logo, the domain and the Merchant Center business name.
_domain: e.g. 'wonderleaf.co.uk'. USE A NEW DOMAIN, not the one that was on Shopify when the misrepresentation suspension happened - enforcement attaches to the website as well as the account, so the old domain carries the history. A .co.uk reads correctly for a UK business. Never a free subdomain.
_legal_name: The exact registered company name at Companies House, including 'Limited' or 'Ltd' exactly as registered.
_company_number: The 8-character Companies House number. Required on the website by the Companies Act 2006 and the E-Commerce Regulations 2002 - this is a legal duty, not only a Google one.
_vat_number: e.g. 'GB123456789'. You said you are VAT registered, so this must appear on the site and all displayed prices must INCLUDE VAT. Google requires VAT-inclusive prices for the UK.
_registered_address: The full registered office address, as an array of lines, ending with the postcode. A real address. Google's policy explicitly prohibits 'using a false or virtual address as headquarters while operating from an undisclosed region'.
_trading_address_same: Set false and fill trading_address if goods are dispatched from somewhere other than the registered office. Google prohibits 'hiding where products ship from'.
_email: A real monitored mailbox ON THE DOMAIN, e.g. 'hello@wonderleaf.co.uk'. Not gmail, not hotmail - a free mailbox on a shop claiming to be a registered company is a trust signal failure and several suspension guides name it directly.
_phone: A working UK telephone number that a person answers or that has voicemail. Google's 'present a false identity, business name, or contact information' rule covers a dead number.
support_hours: Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm UK time

fulfilment._dispatch_working_days: Matches the eBay DispatchTimeMax of 3 that you already run. Do not shorten it to look better: 'hiding processing delays behind a stated delivery time' is listed under dishonest transaction conditions.

delivery.name: UK standard delivery
delivery._price: Set to 0 (free UK delivery) by default on 25 Oct. Reasoning: on a GBP 24.99-34.99 framed print free delivery converts better than a GBP 4.95 line, it makes the feed's shipping attribute trivially correct, and it removes the undisclosed-delivery-cost risk entirely. Change it to a number if you would rather charge - the site, the feed, the checkout and the policy pages all read this one value, so nothing else needs touching.

fulfilment._ships_to: Start UK only. Every extra country is another set of delivery times, tax rules and return-freight disclosures to get right, and getting them wrong is a misrepresentation finding.
fulfilment._paper: The seller's own spec, given 26 Oct. Every page, every feed description and the FAQ read this one value - they used to each carry their own hardcoded 'heavyweight matte art paper', twelve copies, which is how a page and a feed drift apart. If the stock changes, change it here and rebuild. Do not add a gsm or the word archival unless the seller states them: an unsupported material claim is the cheapest way to earn a misrepresentation finding.
fulfilment._inks: Seller's spec, 26 Oct. Pigment rather than dye is a real and checkable difference and worth saying; 'archival' and any fade-resistance rating are not claimed because nobody has tested these prints to one.

returns._window_days: 30 days from DELIVERY, not from order. Google flags 'starting international return windows at purchase date instead of delivery date'. 30 beats the statutory 14 and is worth the goodwill. Whatever is promised here must actually be honoured - 'denying return and refund for a product despite having a clear refund or return policy' is an egregious violation with no warning.
returns._who_pays_return_postage: 'customer' or 'us'. Must be stated plainly on the returns page either way - undisclosed return shipping cost is listed under dishonest pricing.

social_proof._reviews: KEEP THIS AS 'none-yet' UNTIL REAL REVIEWS EXIST. No star ratings, no 'loved by 10,000 customers', no invented bestseller badges, no countdown timers on prices that never expire. Fake reviews became a criminal matter in the UK under the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024, and on Google's side invented social proof sits under misrepresentation. A new shop with no reviews is normal; a new shop with 400 five-star reviews is a suspension.

_order_confirmation_email: Set to true ONLY after you have switched on 'Successful payments' email receipts in the Stripe dashboard (Settings -> Customer emails). The order-confirmed page tells the buyer an email is coming; if Stripe is not sending one then the site is making a statement that is not true, which is the definition of the problem this whole build exists to avoid. preflight fails while this is false.
